content.comment_body: Good evening everyone, I'm [user_name] and new to this community, though I've followed it for a while. I'm working on some small projects using [product_name], and I've run into an issue. I want to use the webserver interface provided by [product_name], but I can't seem to display decimal values for analog variables. For example: Variable AM7 -> value 367 (which I can show as 3.67 on the [product_name] operator panel using certain function blocks). On the custom webserver page, this appears to be impossible. Is this a limitation of [product_name], or am I missing something? I notice that [company_name] offers this on the operator panel but not in the webserver. Any help would be appreciated. Thank you, [user_name]
You have recognized this correctly. At present, it isn't possible to set decimal places for analog values using the Web Editor. I've also found this quite frustrating.

Good morning, with the assistance of two friends who know their way around HTML and JavaScript, I managed to create a temporary workaround. I simply divided the analog values by 100 and forced two decimals in the display. This approach applies to all analog values automatically, which suits my situation for now. We plan further tests to try to modify just the affected variables. [user_name]
That workaround is good, but users like myself who aren't comfortable with HTML won't benefit. And [company_name] always advertises that configuration can be done in just ten minutes...
Can you explain how you did this?

Hi everyone, I needed the same feature. It's quite simple: 1) Open your web page generated by the Web Editor (like main.htm) in a text editor. 2) At the end of the file, find the JavaScript line: var value = getValueByBlockFormat(blockFormat, accessModeType, this.m_sValue); (this is the value for the analog value component). 3) Change it to: var value = getValueByBlockFormat(blockFormat, accessModeType, this.m_sValue) / 10; Now the value gets divided by 10. You can adjust all component values as needed (conversion, calibration, etc.). 4) Save the file and upload it to your SD card. 5) That's all.

I solved it similarly. After the command you've described, there's the command 'actVal = value;'. I changed this to 'actVal = (value/10).toFixed(1);' or 'actVal = (value/100).toFixed(2);'. Note that this only works for read-only values, not values you want to edit, as the modification only works in one direction. See the German forum on page 2: 'Kommazahlen...' [url]
Thanks, [user_name]. I didn't realize this thread existed. Yes, it's a real shame the Editor is currently so limited, but maybe we’ll think of a better solution.

Thanks for the compliment. I'll answer in English here. Normally, it's not our responsibility to solve issues resulting from missing options in the Web Editor. Personally, I just try things out for fun since I don't need the Web Editor for my own projects yet. Hopefully, [company_name] offers a better version next time. Regards, [user_name]
You're right. At least it motivated me to try something better. Hopefully, this helps someone. Thanks for the ideas.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members discussed a key limitation in [product_name] Web Editor: analog values cannot be displayed as decimals, whereas operator panels allow this. Technically skilled users managed to create custom solutions by editing HTML/JavaScript, but this method is inaccessible to those without coding experience. The absence of an integrated way to format analog values as decimals causes frustration, especially as [company_name] claims that fast, simple configuration is possible.
analysis.user_expectations: Members want to display analog values with decimals on the [product_name] Web Editor web interface, just like on the operator panels. They expect a straightforward, user-friendly solution that does not require programming skills.
